# Ratecard — full rate card

99 models, 70 verified, 14 providers. Last checked 2026-11-07. License CC BY 4.0.

## Providers
### OpenAI
- id: openai
- summary: Batch / Flex tier at 50%. Fast mode 2x. Fine-tuning closed to new users.
- source: https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing
- checked: 2026-10-30

### Anthropic
- id: anthropic
- summary: Batch API 50% off. Cache hits 0.025x–0.1x input depending on model.
- source: https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/about-claude/pricing
- checked: 2026-10-30

### Google
- id: google
- summary: Free tier on many Flash models (data may be used to improve products). Batch 50% off. Gemini API pricing page shows 'Last updated 2026-10-30 UTC' (checked 2026-10-31). Google Cloud Agent Platform: from 2026-11-13, Gemini 4 completions over 32K tokens are billed for retrievable tokens even if the request times out.
- source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing
- checked: 2026-10-31

### xAI
- id: xai
- summary: grok-4.7: long-context tier above 200K tokens (2x); Batch API 20% off.
- source: https://docs.x.ai/docs/models
- checked: 2026-10-31

### DeepSeek
- id: deepseek
- summary: Off-peak pricing ~50% of peak. Search and Fetch APIs: $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests each (standalone APIs billed per request); server-side tool calls via DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and Codex billed from 00:00 Beijing time 2026-11-01.
- source: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing
- checked: 2026-10-31

### Together
- id: together
- summary: 
- source: https://www.together.ai/pricing
- checked: 2026-10-30

### Fireworks
- id: fireworks
- summary: 
- source: https://docs.fireworks.ai/serverless/pricing
- checked: 2026-10-30

### Groq
- id: groq
- summary: Developer plan rate limits published per model.
- source: https://console.groq.com/docs/models
- checked: 2026-10-30

### Perplexity
- id: perplexity
- summary: Search tool calls billed per 1K invocations.
- source: https://docs.perplexity.ai/getting-started/models
- checked: 2026-10-30

### Cohere
- id: cohere
- summary: 
- source: https://cohere.com/pricing
- checked: 2026-10-30

### Azure OpenAI
- id: azure-openai
- summary: Global vs Data Zone deployments priced separately.
- source: https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/cognitive-services/openai-service/
- checked: 2026-10-30

### AWS Bedrock
- id: aws-bedrock
- summary: Prices vary by region and cross-region inference type.
- source: https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/
- checked: 2026-10-30

### Mistral

### OpenRouter

## Billing rule changes
- 2026-11-01 (00:00 Beijing time on 2026-11-01 (= 2026-10-31 16:00 UTC)) · DeepSeek · Server-side Search/Fetch tool calls made through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and Codex (direct Search and Fetch API calls are standalone APIs, already billed per request): Agent server-side Search and Fetch tool calls, free until then, start per-request billing. Direct Search/Fetch API calls were never in the free period. Price: $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests (Search); $0.75 per 1,000 successful requests (Fetch) · source https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing (checked 2026-10-31)
- 2026-11-13 (2026-11-13) · Google · Gemini 4 (incl. Gemini 4 Argon) on Google Cloud Agent Platform: When a completion exceeds 32K tokens, retrievable token usage is charged even if the request ultimately fails due to client or server timeouts (today only 200 responses are charged). Price: Standard token rates for retrievable tokens · source https://cloud.google.com/model-garden/pricing (checked 2026-10-31)
- Promotion window · OpenAI gpt-5.6-sol: $4.00 in / $20.00 out per 1M tokens (promotional), at least through 2026-11-21; new price not yet published · source https://platform.openai.com/docs/pricing


## DeepSeek Search & Fetch tool fees (checked 2026-10-31)
Page: https://ratecardai.pages.dev/guides/deepseek-search-fetch-pricing
- Q: What does DeepSeek web search cost per request?
  A: DeepSeek charges $0.75 per 1,000 successful Search API requests and $0.75 per 1,000 successful Fetch API requests, i.e. $0.00075 per request. Both are standalone APIs billed per successful request, not per token or per result returned. The only free usage was server-side tool calls made through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and Codex, which are billed from 00:00 Beijing time on 2026-11-01 (2026-10-31 16:00 UTC, 12:00 PM ET). Source: DeepSeek pricing page and Search & Fetch guide, checked 2026-10-31.
- Q: Which DeepSeek tool requests are billed?
  A: Only requests that return HTTP 200 with a result: Search must return a non-empty results array and Fetch must return page content. Failed requests, empty search results and timeouts are not billed, and the count parameter (1-50 results) does not change the per-request price. Source: DeepSeek Search & Fetch guide, checked 2026-10-31.
- Q: Were DeepSeek Search and Fetch API calls ever free?
  A: Not as direct API calls: DeepSeek describes Search and Fetch as standalone APIs billed per successful request. The free period applied only to server-side tool calls made through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code and Codex, which DeepSeek bills from 00:00 Beijing time on 2026-11-01 (16:00 UTC / 12:00 PM ET on 2026-10-31). Correction 2026-10-31: an earlier version of this page implied all Search/Fetch billing started on that date.
- Q: How much do 100,000 DeepSeek searches cost?
  A: 100,000 successful Search requests cost $75.00. 1,000,000 cost $750.00. Fetch is billed at the same rate, separately.
- Q: Do DeepSeek off-peak discounts apply to Search and Fetch?
  A: DeepSeek’s pricing page lists one flat Search/Fetch price; its “off-peak rates are half of the peak rates” note is attached to the token price table. We model tool fees at the flat rate at all hours.
- Per 1,000/10,000/100,000/1,000,000 successful requests: $0.7500 / $7.50 / $75.00 / $750.00 (per API).


## OpenAI + Anthropic cache-write pricing (checked 2026-11-07)
Page: https://ratecardai.pages.dev/guides/openai-anthropic-cache-write-pricing
- Q: Do OpenAI cache writes cost extra?
  A: OpenAI and Anthropic both charge for prompt cache writes. OpenAI (GPT-5.6+): 30-minute writes are published on the pricing table (gpt-6-astra $12.50 / 1M) and 12-hour writes are 2.5× uncached input ($25.00 / 1M for astra) per the prompt-caching guide — these are total write rates, not a surcharge on top of input. Anthropic: 5-minute writes are 1.25× input and 1-hour writes are 2× input (Claude Sonnet 5.5 $2.50 / $4.00 per 1M). Cached reads stay cheaper (OpenAI typically 0.1× input; Anthropic 0.1× with model-specific exceptions). Ratecard stores absolute $/1M on each model row and the calculator adds Cache-write MTok/mo when you enter a volume. Checked 2026-11-07.
- Q: What is gpt-6-astra cache-write pricing?
  A: As of 2026-11-07, OpenAI lists gpt-6-astra cache writes at $12.50 per 1M tokens for the 30-minute TTL and $25.00 per 1M for the 12-hour TTL (2.5× its $10 input). Long-context (>272K) writes are $25.00 / $50.00. Source: OpenAI pricing table + prompt-caching guide.
- Q: What does Anthropic charge for cache writes?
  A: Anthropic bills 1.25× base input for a 5-minute cache write and 2× base input for a 1-hour write. Example (checked 2026-11-07): Claude Sonnet 5.5 input $2 → 5m $2.50, 1h $4.00 per 1M. Cache reads are typically 0.1× input (0.05× on Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5; 0.025× on Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1). Source: Anthropic pricing docs.
- Q: How do I model cache writes in the Ratecard calculator?
  A: Enter Cache-write tokens / month (M) and pick a TTL (Auto uses the short TTL). The write line uses the published absolute $/1M when the model has fields; otherwise it shows N/A. Write rates are total rates — enter only tokens billed as writes, not also in uncached input. Taxes and negotiated discounts are still excluded.
- Q: Does Claude’s newer tokenizer change cache-write prices?
  A: No. Anthropic notes that Claude 4.7+ (and Mythos Preview) use a tokenizer that produces about 30% more tokens for the same text, which raises billable token counts — it does not change the $/1M cache-write multipliers (still 1.25× / 2× input). Verify token counts on your own prompts.
